```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Thorsted et al. (2026) pooled three Phase I and four Phase III studies of
depemokimab, an ultra-long-acting anti-IL-5 monoclonal antibody given
subcutaneously (SC) twice a year, to build:

1. a population PK model: one compartment with first-order absorption and
   first-order elimination (Supplementary Figure S1, Table S3), and
2. a sequential PK/PD model of the blood eosinophil count (BEC): an
   indirect-response model in which depemokimab inhibits eosinophil production
   through a sigmoid Emax function, on top of a placebo baseline that drifts
   linearly with time (Supplementary Figure S4, Table S4).

The authors fitted the PK/PD model on individual predicted concentrations of
the final PK model. The packaged model `Thorsted_2026_depemokimab` carries both
layers, so one solve gives the concentration `Cc` (ug/mL) and the count
`blood_eosinophils` (cells/uL).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Thorsted_2026_depemokimab"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70187>

# Population

The PK analysis included 961 participants with 9383 concentrations (Table 1):
36 adults with mild-to-moderate asthma in the first-time-in-human (FTIH)
ascending-dose study 205722 (single SC doses of 2-300 mg), 20 healthy Chinese
volunteers (study 208021) and 140 healthy US volunteers (study 214099) given a
single 100 mg or 300 mg dose, and 493 type 2 asthma (SWIFT-1/-2) and 272 CRSwNP
(ANCHOR-1/-2) patients given 100 mg every 26 weeks. Mean age was 49.8 years
(range 12-93), mean weight 78.0 kg (34.6-161) and 19% were Asian. The PK/PD
analysis included 1324 participants on depemokimab or placebo from the FTIH,
SWIFT-1/-2 and ANCHOR-1/-2 studies, with 14,273 counts and a mean baseline
count of 440 cells/uL (Table 3). Healthy volunteers were not part of the PK/PD
analysis.

# Model

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Thorsted_2026_depemokimab")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
theta <- ui$theta
```

# Virtual cohort

Each of the five PK data sources is represented by 200 virtual subjects given
two 100 mg SC doses 26 weeks apart. Table 2 derives the second-interval
exposure of the single-dose Phase I subjects by assuming a second dose at Day
182, so all five cohorts use the same regimen. Covariates are drawn from the
Table 1 means and SDs of each study (weight log-normal, the others normal,
all clipped to the Table 1 range where given); race and injection site are
drawn with the Table 1 proportions.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_per <- 200

study_spec <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study,       ~age, ~age_sd, ~age_lo, ~age_hi, ~wt,  ~wt_sd, ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~alb, ~alb_sd, ~egfr, ~egfr_sd, ~p_asian, ~p_arm, ~p_thigh, ~hv, ~crswnp, ~ftih, ~china,
  "FTIH",       43.9, 10.6,    20,      63,      82.7, 10.2,   64.6,   107,     44.2, 2.36,    100,   12.0,     0.03,     1.00,   0.00,     0,   0,       1,     0,
  "China HV",   29.7, 6.4,     20.9,    43.5,    63.7, 7.21,   50.9,   79.5,    46.4, 1.69,    103,   10.9,     1.00,     1.00,   0.00,     1,   0,       0,     1,
  "US HV",      35.5, 8.0,     18,      50,      72.6, 11.0,   51.3,   101,     45.2, 3.02,    104,   17.6,     0.05,     0.34,   0.34,     1,   0,       0,     0,
  "SWIFT-1/-2", 53.7, 14.8,    12,      82,      79.2, 19.7,   34.6,   161,     45.4, 3.05,    89.5,  19.1,     0.18,     0.95,   0.05,     0,   0,       0,     0,
  "ANCHOR-1/-2", 52.4, 13.3,   20,      93,      79.0, 16.0,   45.9,   145,     45.8, 3.13,    92.2,  15.3,     0.24,     0.95,   0.05,     0,   1,       0,     0
)

draw_lognormal <- function(n, mean, sd) {
  sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (sd / mean)^2))
  exp(rnorm(n, log(mean) - sdlog^2 / 2, sdlog))
}

draw_study <- function(spec, id_offset) {
  site <- sample(c("arm", "thigh", "abdomen"), n_per, replace = TRUE,
                 prob = c(spec$p_arm, spec$p_thigh, max(0, 1 - spec$p_arm - spec$p_thigh)))
  data.frame(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_per),
    study = spec$study,
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per, spec$age, spec$age_sd), spec$age_lo), spec$age_hi),
    WT = pmin(pmax(draw_lognormal(n_per, spec$wt, spec$wt_sd), spec$wt_lo), spec$wt_hi),
    ALB = rnorm(n_per, spec$alb, spec$alb_sd),
    CRCL = rnorm(n_per, spec$egfr, spec$egfr_sd),
    RACE_ASIAN = rbinom(n_per, 1, spec$p_asian),
    INJSITE_ARM = as.integer(site == "arm"),
    INJSITE_THIGH = as.integer(site == "thigh"),
    DIS_HEALTHY = spec$hv,
    DIS_CHRONIC_RHINOSINUSITIS_NASAL_POLYPS = spec$crswnp,
    STUDY_205722 = spec$ftih,
    STUDY_208021 = spec$china,
    DOSE_LOW = 0
  )
}

cohort <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(study_spec)), function(i) {
  draw_study(study_spec[i, ], id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(cohort$id))

obs_days <- 0:364
make_events <- function(cov, dose_times, dose_amt) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(id = cov$id, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_amt, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(id = cov$id, time = obs_days) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "blood_eosinophils")
  dplyr::bind_rows(obs, doses) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, evid)
}
events <- make_events(cohort, dose_times = c(0, 182), dose_amt = 100)
```

Observation rows sit on the `blood_eosinophils` state; rxode2 still returns
`Cc` at each of them.

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events, keep = "study", returnType = "data.frame")
```

# PK: individual parameters (Table 2)

Table 2 reports geometric means of the individually predicted CL/F, V/F, ka
and Frel per study. The simulated individual parameters are compared with them
below.

```{r pk-params}
geo <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))
indiv <- sim |>
  dplyr::group_by(id, study) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cl_f = cl[1], v_f = vc[1],
                   ka = ka[1], frel = fdepot[1], .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(thalf = log(2) * v_f / cl_f)

published_par <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study,        ~cl_f, ~v_f, ~ka,  ~frel, ~thalf,
  "FTIH",        0.113, 6.44, 0.38, 0.88,  39.4,
  "China HV",    0.063, 5.63, 0.60, 1.05,  62.0,
  "US HV",       0.091, 5.76, 0.41, 0.97,  44.0,
  "SWIFT-1/-2",  0.093, 6.53, 0.20, 1.01,  48.6,
  "ANCHOR-1/-2", 0.100, 6.59, 0.20, 0.95,  45.8
)

par_cmp <- indiv |>
  dplyr::group_by(study) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(cl_f, v_f, ka, frel, thalf), geo), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-study, names_to = "parameter", values_to = "simulated") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(published_par, -study, names_to = "parameter", values_to = "published"),
    by = c("study", "parameter")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / published - 1))

par_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(study = factor(study, levels = study_spec$study)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(study, parameter) |>
  dplyr::rename(Study = study, Parameter = parameter, Simulated = simulated,
                "Thorsted 2026 Table 2" = published, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = paste(
    "Geometric means of individual PK parameters (CL/F and V/F in L/day and L,",
    "ka in 1/day, t1/2 in days)."
  ))
```

The parameters that carry the covariate model (CL/F, V/F and the half-life)
match closely. Table 2 reports CL/F and V/F as the model parameters
themselves (apparent values for Frel = 1), not divided by the individual
relative bioavailability, so the simulated values are compared the same way.

```{r pk-params-check}
structural <- dplyr::filter(par_cmp, parameter %in% c("cl_f", "v_f", "thalf"))
stopifnot(
  abs(median(structural$pct_diff)) < 5,
  max(abs(structural$pct_diff)) < 15
)
```

# PK: concentration-time profiles

```{r pk-profile, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
pk_summary <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0) |>
  dplyr::group_by(study, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
                   .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pk_summary, aes(time / 7, med, colour = study, fill = study)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "Depemokimab (ug/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Median and 90% interval, 100 mg SC at Weeks 0 and 26",
       caption = "Compare with Figure 1 and Supplementary Figure S2 of Thorsted 2026.")
```

# PKNCA validation (Table 2 secondary parameters)

Table 2 reports the second-interval (Weeks 26-52) Cmax, Tmax and AUCtau,ss and
the troughs at Weeks 26 and 52. PKNCA computes them per study over the two
dosing intervals.

```{r pknca}
conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, study, time, Cc)
dose_df <- events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, study, time, amt)

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | study + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | study + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 182), end = c(182, 364),
  cmax = c(FALSE, TRUE), tmax = c(FALSE, TRUE), auclast = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  clast.obs = TRUE
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)
```

```{r nca-compare}
second <- nca_res |> dplyr::filter(start == 182)
first_trough <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::filter(start == 0, PPTESTCD == "clast.obs") |>
  dplyr::mutate(PPTESTCD = "ctrough")
nca_both <- dplyr::bind_rows(second, first_trough)

published_nca <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study,        ~cmax, ~tmax, ~auclast, ~clast.obs, ~ctrough,
  "FTIH",        12.29, 8.41,  778.8,    0.606,      0.585,
  "China HV",    19.50, 6.56,  1661,     2.779,      2.463,
  "US HV",       15.62, 8.05,  1071,     1.041,      0.987,
  "SWIFT-1/-2",  13.63, 13.59, 1081,     1.315,      1.227,
  "ANCHOR-1/-2", 12.46, 13.42, 950.3,    1.041,      0.982
)

nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_both, reference = published_nca, by = "study",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", tmax = "day", auclast = "ug*day/mL",
            clast.obs = "ug/mL", ctrough = "ug/mL")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste(
    "Simulated medians vs Thorsted 2026 Table 2 geometric means (100 mg at Weeks 0 and 26).",
    "AUClast is AUCtau,ss over Weeks 26-52, Clast is the Week 52 trough and Ctrough the Week 26 trough.",
    "* marks a difference above 20%."
  ))
```

```{r nca-check}
nca_cmp <- nca_both |>
  dplyr::group_by(study, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    tidyr::pivot_longer(published_nca, -study, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "pub"),
    by = c("study", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (sim / pub - 1))
exposure <- dplyr::filter(nca_cmp, PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast", "clast.obs", "ctrough"))
stopifnot(
  nrow(exposure) == 20,
  abs(median(exposure$pct)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(exposure$pct), 0.9) < 25
)
```

# PK/PD: structure checks

The paper writes the eosinophil state as the count relative to the placebo
count, R, with `dR/dt = kout * (1 - inh) - kout * R` and `R(0) = 1`, where
`inh = Emax * C^hill / (C^hill + EC50^hill)`, and the placebo count is
`BL * (1 + Pslp * t)`. The packaged state is the absolute count
`B = BL * (1 + Pslp * t) * R`, which needs the product rule. Two checks pin that
rewrite: a placebo subject must follow the linear placebo line exactly, and a
treated subject's ratio to that line must equal R from the paper's own
equation, solved separately here.

```{r structure-check}
typ <- data.frame(
  WT = 77.4, AGE = 54, ALB = 45, CRCL = 94, RACE_ASIAN = 0, INJSITE_ARM = 1,
  INJSITE_THIGH = 0, DIS_HEALTHY = 0, DIS_CHRONIC_RHINOSINUSITIS_NASAL_POLYPS = 0,
  STUDY_205722 = 0, STUDY_208021 = 0, DOSE_LOW = 0
)
ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  make_events(cbind(id = 1L, typ), dose_times = c(0, 182), dose_amt = 100),
  make_events(cbind(id = 2L, typ), dose_times = numeric(0), dose_amt = 0)
)
typ_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_typ, omega = NA, sigma = NA, returnType = "data.frame")

placebo <- dplyr::filter(typ_sim, id == 2)
placebo_line <- exp(theta[["lrbase"]]) * (1 + theta[["slope_placebo"]] * placebo$time / 365.25)
stopifnot(max(abs(placebo$blood_eosinophils / placebo_line - 1)) < 1e-5)

ratio_model <- rxode2::rxode2({
  d/dt(depot) <- -ka * depot
  d/dt(central) <- ka * depot - kel * central
  C <- central / vc
  inh <- emax * C^hill / (C^hill + ec50^hill)
  d/dt(ratio) <- kout * (1 - inh) - kout * ratio
  ratio(0) <- 1
})
treated <- dplyr::filter(typ_sim, id == 1)
ratio_pars <- c(ka = treated$ka[1], kel = treated$kel[1], vc = treated$vc[1],
                emax = treated$emax[1], hill = treated$hill[1],
                ec50 = treated$ec50[1], kout = treated$kout[1])
ratio_ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 100 * treated$fdepot[1], time = c(0, 182), cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(obs_days)
ratio_sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ratio_model, ratio_pars, ratio_ev))
ratio_packaged <- treated$blood_eosinophils /
  (treated$rbase * (1 + treated$slope_pbo * treated$time / 365.25))
stopifnot(max(abs(ratio_packaged - ratio_sim$ratio)) < 1e-4)
```

# PK/PD: replicate Figure 4

Figure 4 shows the typical Week-52 percent reduction in BEC relative to
placebo after 100 mg every 26 weeks for a reference non-Asian SWIFT asthma
participant (predicted baseline 317 cells/uL, 54 years, 77.4 kg) and
univariate covariate changes. The percent reduction is `100 * (1 - R)` at Day
364. A different predicted baseline is set through `lrbase`, because the
baseline effect on Emax acts on the individual predicted baseline.

```{r fig4}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario,                  ~RACE_ASIAN, ~crswnp, ~ftih, ~bl,  ~AGE, ~WT,   ~published,
  "Asian in ANCHOR",          1,           1,       0,     317,  54,   77.4,  85.6,
  "Non-Asian in ANCHOR",      0,           1,       0,     317,  54,   77.4,  82.9,
  "Asian in SWIFT",           1,           0,       0,     317,  54,   77.4,  86.3,
  "Non-Asian in SWIFT",       0,           0,       0,     317,  54,   77.4,  81.0,
  "FTIH",                     0,           0,       1,     317,  54,   77.4,  81.9,
  "Baseline 684 cells/uL",    0,           0,       0,     684,  54,   77.4,  87.3,
  "Baseline 151 cells/uL",    0,           0,       0,     151,  54,   77.4,  71.6,
  "Age 70 years",             0,           0,       0,     317,  70,   77.4,  82.2,
  "Age 33 years",             0,           0,       0,     317,  33,   77.4,  79.1,
  "Weight 102.9 kg",          0,           0,       0,     317,  54,   102.9, 77.9,
  "Weight 58 kg",             0,           0,       0,     317,  54,   58,    83.2
)

fig4_sim <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fig4)), function(i) {
  cv <- typ
  cv$RACE_ASIAN <- fig4$RACE_ASIAN[i]
  cv$DIS_CHRONIC_RHINOSINUSITIS_NASAL_POLYPS <- fig4$crswnp[i]
  cv$STUDY_205722 <- fig4$ftih[i]
  cv$AGE <- fig4$AGE[i]
  cv$WT <- fig4$WT[i]
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = c(0, 182, 364), evid = c(1L, 1L, 0L),
                   amt = c(100, 100, 0), cmt = c("depot", "depot", "blood_eosinophils")) |>
    cbind(cv)
  pars <- theta
  pars[["lrbase"]] <- log(fig4$bl[i])
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = pars, omega = NA, sigma = NA,
                       returnType = "data.frame")
  r <- s$blood_eosinophils[s$time == 364] / (s$rbase[1] * (1 + s$slope_pbo[1] * 364 / 365.25))
  100 * (1 - r)
}, numeric(1))

fig4_cmp <- fig4 |>
  dplyr::mutate(simulated = fig4_sim, difference = simulated - published)
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, published, simulated, difference) |>
  dplyr::rename(Scenario = scenario, "Thorsted 2026 Figure 4 (%)" = published,
                "Typical-value simulation (%)" = simulated,
                "Difference (percentage points)" = difference) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Week-52 BEC reduction from placebo, 100 mg every 26 weeks.")
```

Every scenario reproduces the published median within about half a percentage
point. The published points are medians over parameter uncertainty, so a small
offset from the typical value is expected.

```{r fig4-check}
stopifnot(max(abs(fig4_cmp$difference)) < 1.5)
```

# PK/PD: replicate Figure 5

Figure 5 shows the steady-state BEC ratio of placebo for a concentration held
constant, `1 - Emax * C^hill / (C^hill + EC50^hill)`, for typical participants
of each study population. The curves below use the reference covariates of
Table S4 (54 years, 77.4 kg, baseline 317 cells/uL) for each population; the
paper does not state which covariates it used for the FTIH curve.

```{r fig5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
expit <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
emax_of <- function(crswnp) {
  expit(theta[["logitemax"]] +
    theta[["e_dis_chronic_rhinosinusitis_nasal_polyps_emax"]] * crswnp)
}
pop <- data.frame(
  population = c("SWIFT-1/-2", "ANCHOR-1/-2", "FTIH Asthma study"),
  emax = c(emax_of(0), emax_of(1), emax_of(0)),
  ec50 = exp(theta[["lec50"]]) * c(1, 1, 1 + theta[["e_study_205722_ec50"]])
)
hill <- exp(theta[["lhill"]])
conc_grid <- 10^seq(-2, 2, by = 0.02)
fig5 <- tidyr::crossing(pop, conc = conc_grid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio = 1 - emax * conc^hill / (conc^hill + ec50^hill))

ggplot(fig5, aes(conc, ratio, colour = population)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "Depemokimab concentration (ug/mL)", y = "Model-predicted BEC ratio of placebo",
       colour = NULL, title = "Replicates Figure 5 of Thorsted 2026")

knitr::kable(
  dplyr::mutate(pop, floor = 1 - emax,
                ec90 = ec50 * 9^(1 / hill)) |>
    dplyr::rename(Population = population, Emax = emax, "EC50 (ug/mL)" = ec50,
                  "Ratio at saturation" = floor, "EC90 (ug/mL)" = ec90),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Typical Emax and potency; EC90 is the concentration giving 90% of Emax."
)
```

# PK/PD: blood eosinophil time course and trough potency

The SWIFT-1/-2 and ANCHOR-1/-2 cohorts above received 100 mg at Weeks 0 and 26;
placebo arms of 200 subjects each are added from the same covariate
distributions. The plot shows the BEC ratio to each subject's baseline
(compare with Figure 3 and Supplementary Figure S5).

```{r pd-placebo}
placebo_cov <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  draw_study(study_spec[4, ], id_offset = 5000L),
  draw_study(study_spec[5, ], id_offset = 6000L)
)
placebo_ev <- make_events(placebo_cov, dose_times = numeric(0), dose_amt = 0)
sim_pbo <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, placebo_ev, keep = "study", returnType = "data.frame")

pd <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim |> dplyr::filter(study %in% c("SWIFT-1/-2", "ANCHOR-1/-2")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(arm = "Depemokimab 100 mg Q26W"),
  sim_pbo |> dplyr::mutate(arm = "Placebo")
) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ratio_bl = blood_eosinophils / blood_eosinophils[time == 0]) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r pd-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
pd_summary <- pd |>
  dplyr::group_by(study, arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(med = median(ratio_bl), lo = quantile(ratio_bl, 0.05),
                   hi = quantile(ratio_bl, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
ggplot(pd_summary, aes(time / 7, med, colour = arm, fill = arm)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~study) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Week", y = "BEC ratio to baseline", colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "Median and 90% interval of individual predictions")
```

The paper reports that 100 mg reduced the count to below 25% of baseline,
with a small rise before the Week 26 dose, and that the reduction relative to
placebo stayed close to 80% at Week 52. It also reports that at Week 52 every
Phase III participant had a trough above the EC50, and that 94% (SWIFT-1/-2)
and 83% (ANCHOR-1/-2) had troughs above the EC90.

```{r pd-check}
pd_week <- pd |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(28, 180, 364)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(study, arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_ratio = median(ratio_bl), .groups = "drop")
pd_week |>
  dplyr::rename(Study = study, Arm = arm, Day = time, "Median ratio to baseline" = median_ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Median BEC ratio to baseline at Days 28, 180 and 364.")

placebo_corrected <- pd_week |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 364) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = median_ratio) |>
  dplyr::mutate(reduction_pct = 100 * (1 - `Depemokimab 100 mg Q26W` / Placebo))
placebo_corrected |>
  dplyr::select(-time) |>
  dplyr::rename(Study = study, "Reduction vs placebo (%)" = reduction_pct) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Week-52 median ratio to baseline and reduction relative to placebo (ratio of median ratios).")

troughs <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(study %in% c("SWIFT-1/-2", "ANCHOR-1/-2"), time == 364) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ec90 = ec50 * 9^(1 / hill)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(study) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pct_above_ec50 = 100 * mean(Cc > ec50),
                   pct_above_ec90 = 100 * mean(Cc > ec90), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(published_above_ec90 = c("ANCHOR-1/-2" = 83, "SWIFT-1/-2" = 94)[study])
troughs |>
  dplyr::rename(Study = study, "Above EC50 (%)" = pct_above_ec50, "Above EC90 (%)" = pct_above_ec90,
                "Thorsted 2026, above EC90 (%)" = published_above_ec90) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Week-52 troughs above the individual EC50 and EC90.")

treated_nadir <- pd_week |>
  dplyr::filter(arm == "Depemokimab 100 mg Q26W", time == 28)
stopifnot(
  all(treated_nadir$median_ratio < 0.25),
  all(abs(placebo_corrected$reduction_pct - 80) < 8),
  all(troughs$pct_above_ec50 > 95),
  # A fraction over 200 subjects has a binomial SE of about 3 percentage
  # points, and the cohort's covariates only approximate Table 1.
  all(abs(troughs$pct_above_ec90 - troughs$published_above_ec90) < 15)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate centring.** Table S3 does not print the centring values of the
  PK covariates. The model uses the reference subject of Figure 2 and
  Supplementary Figure S3 (76 kg, 50 years, albumin 45 g/L, eGFR 94
  mL/min/1.73 m^2), which are the medians of the PK population; the
  Table 2 geometric means are reproduced with it. The PD centring (54 years,
  77.4 kg, predicted baseline 317 cells/uL) is stated in Table S4.
* **Covariate functional forms.** The Supplementary Methods state that
  continuous covariates enter as exponential models and categorical ones as a
  fractional difference from the most common category; Table S3 labels the
  continuous effects "fractional change per unit". The model uses
  `exp(theta * (cov - ref))`; the linear form `1 + theta * (cov - ref)` differs by
  less than 0.5% over the observed albumin and eGFR ranges.
* **Population and study indicators.** Following Table S1 footnote e, the
  healthy-volunteer population effects apply to both healthy-volunteer
  studies (`DIS_HEALTHY = 1`), and the China study adds its own effects
  (`STUDY_208021 = 1`). The FTIH study effects (`STUDY_205722 = 1`) apply on
  top of the asthma population. Table 2's ka of 0.60 /day in the China study
  is reproduced only this way.
* **Injection site.** The paper's reference site is the upper arm and only an
  abdomen effect on ka was estimated. The abdomen indicator is formed as
  `1 - INJSITE_ARM - INJSITE_THIGH`, so the reference subject needs
  `INJSITE_ARM = 1`.
* **Residual error.** Table S3 states that RUV is additive on the log scale
  (reported as an approximate CV). Table S4 gives the eosinophil RUV in the
  same form; it is implemented the same way. Both residual SDs carry an
  exponential between-subject variability. The PK SD is multiplied by 6.18
  for samples taken less than 3 h after a dose, using `tad(depot)`.
* **Placebo slope units.** Pslp is a fractional change per year; the model
  divides time in days by 365.25.
* **Eosinophil state.** The paper integrates the count as a ratio of the
  placebo count (Supplementary Figure S4). The packaged state is the absolute
  count, obtained by the product rule; the structure check above shows the
  two agree to within numerical error.
* **2 mg dose effect.** The 2 mg FTIH cohort's CL/F effect is carried as
  `DOSE_LOW`; it is not used in any simulation here.
* **Not reproduced.** Figures 2 and S3 (univariate covariate effects on PK
  exposure, with uncertainty) and the VPCs (Figure S2, S5) need the observed
  data or the parameter uncertainty and are not reproduced; Table 2 and
  Figure 4 cover the same covariate model.
